data.name: Ongaku
data.detailed_description:
“Pop the bubbles to the music, to paint the perfect picture!”

Ongaku is a uniquely addictive side-scrolling 2D rhythm action game with the infusion of original music and stylised artwork.
Features:

• Help Ongaku match the right colour and steer, for bubbles to pop so paint will appear
• Paint will colour over the black and the white, restoring the picture to a glorious sight
• Simply ‘Scoop’ bubbles for a small score, then ‘tap’ to master and grow your score more
• If things are too easy then step up a gear, 5 difficulties will test your musical ear
• Follow the story to stop Discord’s evil plans, by travelling through 11 magical lands
• Get your music and pictures out of the attic, even videos can plug into the Tune-A-Matic
• Create and share levels, that’s no lie, use the Melody Maker it’s as easy as pie
• So you want a new look then buy one of these, Theme Packs including Dance, Rock and Zombies!

reviews.review:
🎵 Ongaku Review
Overall: ★★☆☆☆ (Mixed)
Hours Played: 0.2

Hey, this is Goldheart, founder of Team SBO. We're currently designing a game and we got inspired by the original Ongaku flash game mechanics for a section of my own. I just learned while talking with the mates that the game I enjoyed playing (even with its flaws on Newgrounds) got remastered and brought to Steam. I was happy with the news, and with the low price point, I bought it immediately. What was installed turned out to be a fever dream the likes of which I was not prepared for.

This game isn't entirely bad but... I'll be honest, it just wasn't what I expected, and the Newgrounds version is a little bit better in my opinion. Still, it has a few improvements to the first game, but I'm going to be extremely critical of this game. You deserve it, the devs deserve it. And if they ever read this and my own project goes live...

I hope they see it one day, and the impact they've had on my life from their initial title.

Here's the official Steam release of Ongaku for PC:

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

🥁 Gameplay
★★☆☆☆
Core mechanics: They remain the same as the first game but with one caveat. Lanes have been completely replaced with a freeform rail and aim assist. You have to be more precise with that scooping and catching than the first game for this reason.
Timing feels: Much better than the first game. All there is to say on the matter.
Fun factor: Eh... Without the lanes the game feels less fun. I don't really like this direction compared to the first.

📈 Progression
☆☆☆☆☆
Unlocks: You have to commit to a difficulty level as you progress. If you play Easy and think "Oh that's too easy, I'd like to try the next level at a higher difficulty", you have to start over with the first track.
Difficulty curve: No comment, I never played all four.
Replay value: I mean... there are level editors and stuff, but I wouldn't want to go back to a track I've cleared. First game was better with that and going for Perfects.

🎮 Controls
★★★☆☆
Responsiveness: Good. The note moves as I expect, and the arrows pop up too.
Input latency: Minimal to none.
Accessibility: There are Classic Controls (Bonus star for that), along with pro and gamepad controls. Not much else to really go into.

🎼 Music
★☆☆☆☆
- Soundtrack quality: Good, no stutters/artifacts
- Variety: Low, the first two tracks felt like they blended together
- Memorability: Very low, same reason

🔊 Audio Quality
☆☆☆☆☆
Mixing: Extremely poor. You hear that evil laugh way too much, like if you do anything wrong, that laugh is going to interrupt everything.
Hit sounds: Were there even any? I didn't really notice normal hit sounds.
Feedback: The "bad hit" feedback is probably the worst I have heard. It cuts out the music and the music interrupts it when you're good again.

🎯 Chart Design
★★☆☆☆
Fairness: Relatively fair, but the vertical positioning is a little unforgiving.
Creativity: About on par with the first game.
Difficulty balance: No comment. I didn't play all difficulties in the short time I've owned it.

🎨 Visuals
★★☆☆☆
Art style: It's a Seuss-esque fever dream with Parappa the Rapper-styled animation quality, and it looks like the first level is similar to the tutorial, which is nice. However, the aesthetic of "painting a picture" is replaced with "floating through murk" and honestly it's a lot less enjoyable.
Readability: Ehhh... A LOT is going on at any one time. Achievements all over the place, tons of "visual rewards" that distract and flood the screen. Also the UI is just a NIGHTMARE.
Effects: Everything is really slow and... floaty. Like too floaty.

📖 Presentation / Story
★★☆☆☆
Characters: You pretty much have Ongaku, the two wizards, a tiger-thing, the big wand, and nothing else that noticeable and memorable.
Dialogue: Hardly any, which tracks with the first game. I wasn't expecting hollywood voice actors or anything.
Worldbuilding: Well, it's there, and there's more of it. Each level has its own story, and the opening cutscene is note for note (pun intended) the first game's, so I like the attention to detail there.

🌐 Features
★★☆☆☆
Mod support: I don't know if Steam Workshop even supports this; did this come out before SWS was a thing?
Custom songs: Tons of support for it. I have seen the editor but haven't used it.
Settings: I never really checked.

🐞 Performance
★★★☆☆
Stability: It's stable. Not a big fan of the hitboxes and the timing.
Load times: Not really much if any.
Bugs: None as far as I could tell.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

👍 Pros
• It's a reimagining of the original game with nothing left out from it in terms of story.
• New control layouts while preserving the old ones.
• Timing has been vastly improved compared to the original.
• If you like trippy fever dreams, you'll love the cutscenes.

👎 Cons
• The new core gameplay isn't as good as the first game.
• The worst SFX in the entire game is recycled in multiple locations.
• This game replaces Percentage Points to unlock stages freely with forced progression and difficulty gates.
• The visuals are a complete eyesore. Way too much is animated and moving all at once.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

💭 Final Thoughts
Honestly, it's worse. This game is an example of showing what things like feature creep can do. The game is expanded, but expanding on something doesn't inherently make it better. There's more to it but it lacks polish, punch, and the game goes in a bunch of different style directions at once. I expected synths and classical music, but got whimsical fantasy music that isn't very memorable, compared to the first game where those tracks are ones I can still remember to this day.

If you have some time, definitely check this game out on Newgrounds and give it a shot there. You'll understand why lane snapping is superior to this despite free sliding making the game harder.

Recommended?
❌ No

Would I Replay It? ★★☆☆☆

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: XP, Vista, Windows 7 or later
  • Processador: 2.4 GHz
  • Memória: 1 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: DirectX 9c, shader 2.0 and 256MB Graphics Memory
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0c
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 2 GB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: DirectX 9 compatible sound card
  • Notas adicionais: Windows Media Player 9 or later, DirectX End-User Runtime Web Installer, Microsoft Visual C++ 2008 Redistributable Package. Videos used in the game need to be maximum 2gb and need to be able to be viewed in Windows Media Player
